newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia picks BAe Hawk trainer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia picks BAe Hawk trainer.

text.p: Australian Defence Minister Ian McLachlan said British Aerospace (BAe) had been chosen as the potential supplier for Australia's Lead-In Fighter project.
"British Aerospace has been selected as the potential supplier (for) a derivative of its Hawk aircraft as the new Lead-In Fighter for the Australian Defence Force," McLachlan said in a statement.
McLachlan did not say how many aircraft would be bought.
The Defence Department has previously said up to 40 aircraft might be involved but it would be up to each tenderer to decide how many would be needed to fulfil the requirement.
BAe's selection as potential tenderer is a preliminary to the negotiation of the final contract.
The company beat Italy's Aeracchi, which had offered its MB.399FD trainer.
McDonnell Douglas Corp, with a U.S. Navy version of the Hawk, was eliminated in September.

"All tenders were of a high quality and British Aerospace's bid was selected after detailed evaluation across a wide range of areas, including aircraft design and performance, costs and Australian industry involvement proposals," McLachlan said.
The value of the project has never been revealed, although analysts have made estimates as high as A$1 billion (US$790 million).
The Hawks, a variant of the Hawk 100 model, will replace elderly Aermacchi MB.326s for introductory training of combat jet pilots and for exercising with the Royal Australian Navy.

BAe has previously said that if selected it would deliver the first 12 aircraft complete and the balance in kits for local assembly at the Williamtown air force base at Newcastle, where the fleet would be maintained.
Hawks are fitted with Rolls-Royce Adour engines, which would be assembled and maintained by Qantas Airways Ltd .
